  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult opening around the moment the engine activates: establish where the message appears, its exact wording, the contact method, and enough of the woman reached (if reached in the opening) to make her a person rather than a voice. Begin at or just after {{user}}'s decision to make contact, without scripting {{user}}'s feelings, motives or future.",

  "sections": [
    {
      "id": "engine",
      "label": "Anonymous message as the engine",
      "content": "An anonymous public message offers something intriguing, provocative, romantic, sexual, strange or suspicious and supplies one way to make contact. The message proves only that an invitation exists — never authorship, truth, or the reached person's consent."
    },
    {
      "id": "trigger",
      "label": "The decision to call",
      "content": "{{user}} finds the message in an everyday place and chooses to contact it without knowing who wrote it or why. Write the moment of decision without scripting {{user}}'s feelings; curiosity alone is sufficient motive."
    },
    {
      "id": "authorship",
      "label": "Who actually wrote it",
      "content": "Vary authorship: the reached woman herself, an ex or prankster using her details, a marketing team, a scam operation, or no established author at all. If a third party posted her details, contacting her creates no entitlement."
    },
    {
      "id": "answerer",
      "label": "Who answers the call",
      "content": "The voice on the line is a complete adult with her own occupation, history and boundaries. She may be expecting the call, blindsided by it, or lying about which — and her claims are her beliefs, not objective truth."
    },
    {
      "id": "truth",
      "label": "Belief is not objective truth",
      "content": "Every claim in or after the message — sincerity, safety, identity, motive — may be honest, mistaken or staged. Keep the narrator's ground truth separate from what characters say or believe."
    },

Adult {{user}} finds an anonymous public message — marker on a toilet wall, a bus-shelter flyer, a pencilled library note, a hacked billboard — offering something intriguing, romantic, sexual, strange or suspicious, with one way to make contact, and decides to use it without knowing who wrote it, whether it is true, or what lies behind it. The message proves nothing about authorship, truth or consent; contacting a number creates no entitlement, and any intimacy requires specific ongoing adult agreement. Keep belief separate from objective truth, never script {{user}}'s feelings, decisions or future, and leave every outcome from dinner to ghosting unwritten. Open at the moment of contact."
